hints.content: The arrow points to all values greater than $-2$.
And the point at $-2$ is filled in.
So, the inequality represents everything **greater than or equal to $-2$.**

question.content:
**Choose the inequality that represents the following graph.**



[[☃ image 1]]

[[☃ radio 2]]

options.alt: A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the right starts at negative 2 and continues right. A closed point is plotted at negative 2 where the line begins.

choices.clue:
The graph of $x < -2$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the left starts at negative 2 and continues left. An open point is plotted at negative 2 where the line begins.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/1595de4043d7b1d606ed55693c29830f5fde4a8e)

The graph of $x \leq -2$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the left starts at negative 2 and continues left. A closed point is plotted at negative 2 where the line begins.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/e9c6a4b064bf27fc1c7072a109b8a17fd586819c)

The graph of $x > -2$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the right starts at negative 2 and continues right. An open point is plotted at negative 2 where the line begins.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/c8f32ea13dfc498d39faaa9d1de925ce2adfd1db)
